before.known: मैं आपकी मदद के बिना नहीं कर पाता लेकिन मैंने सोचा होता।
before.target: I wouldn't have been able to without your help but I'd have thought

problem: R8 tier 2/3: the two clauses are unrelated and the sentence is incoherent in both languages.
evidence: 'I wouldn't have been able to without your help but I'd have thought' has no sensible meaning beside the sibling 'I'd have thought' rows.

before.known: मैं बहुत थका हुआ हूँ लेकिन मैंने और सोचा होता।
before.target: I'm too tired but I'd have thought more

problem: R8: a USE row must be a natural complete sentence; 'too tired but I'd have thought more' is a non sequitur.
evidence: S0566L01 siblings are all 'I think/I'm sure I'd have thought more'; this one joins an unrelated clause.

before.known: यह सच नहीं है कि यह छुट्टियों को बहुत ख़ास बना देती है।
before.target: it isn't true that makes the holidays very special

after.known: क्या आपको लगता है कि यह छुट्टियों को बहुत ख़ास बना देती है?
after.target: do you think that makes the holidays very special?

problem: Grammar: 'it isn't true that makes the holidays...' is ungrammatical, because the subject of 'makes' is missing.
evidence: The LEGO target is 'makes the holidays very special'. After 'that' it needs a subject, as in 'it isn't true that it makes...'.

before.known: आपकी मदद के बिना मैं आपको वापस कॉल करूँगी।
before.target: I'll call you back without your help

problem: R8 tier 2/3: 'I'll call you back without your help' makes no sense.
evidence: Seed 564 means 'without your help' as a condition for ability. Calling back without help is not a coherent meaning.

before.known: हमारे मिलने पर मैं आपको वापस कॉल करूँगी।
before.target: I'll call you back when we meet

problem: R8 tier 2/3: 'I'll call you back when we meet' is incoherent, since you cannot call someone back when you meet them.
evidence: S0568L03 USE row; seed 568 is about expecting to see an improvement when they meet.

before.known: आपकी मदद के बिना मैं बहुत थका हुआ हूँ।
before.target: I'm too tired without your help

problem: R8: 'I'm too tired without your help' is unnatural, and the Hindi 'बहुत थका हुआ' does not match 'too tired'.
evidence: The LEGO is 'without your help'. The sentence has no sensible link between tiredness and help, and the Hindi and English do not match.
